evidence: Workbook row 36 (both sheets): distinctive values the judge creates to prove a mutation must not already sit in the seed or the reference's initial state. Skill ref quality-checks.md:149-151: every distinctive value a criterion tells the judge to create (probe SKU, reason, name) is absent from the seed and reference markup; check-probe-not-in-seed.py owns it (not available/run here; applied manually, not labelled a checker run). Probe inventory: (1) Gates/global browser gate (constraints judge.toml hro_gate_shared; functional/polish/visual prompt 'Global browser gate'): job title, candidate name and email must be 'unique' (suffixed 'for this review'); seed has only titles Platform Engineer/Data Analyst/Product Designer and 16 named applications, so no pre-satisfaction. (2) Functional prompt.md:15 and S/M/L/C/B: all jobs J1/J2 and cards A-F, V-Z are new, titles and names suffixed per review; a seed Applied card cannot satisfy hro_job_open, hro_add_candidate, hro_add_email_rules (A's email is judge-chosen; the same-address control goes to the new J2), moves, bulk, undo or activity rows. Rejection reason for C is judge-typed on a new card; the only seeded reason ('Portfolio did not show shipped product work.') is on Lena's APP-301 in Product Designer, never used in M. (3) Notes (hro_notes, B12 note on A2): new text on new cards; seeded notes are only on APP-101/107/301. (4) Activity (hro_activity, hro_activity_refusals): db.js seedIfEmpty inserts users, jobs, applications, messages, reads, notes only (no activity rows), and the rows filter to the new J1/J2, so seeded activity cannot pre-satisfy. (5) Conversations T/U/K: a new J2 card with tomas.varga@candidates.example creates a new conversation; seed links Tomas only to APP-201 Data Analyst (seed applications), and hro_candidate_linked requires the new suffixed J2 application to appear, which the seeded Data Analyst one cannot satisfy; fallback to the seeded conversation reads counts 'relative to their values before you act' (prompt T). Messages, replay sends ('with new text'), Shift+Enter text are judge-authored; seeded APP-201/301/302 bodies are fixed generic lines. hro_thread_access replays require 'new text' so a seeded message cannot count as 'added'. (6) Polish: example draft 'Call back on Fri' and 'distinctive' replies; grep over solution and environment finds no 'Call back' string and the seed has no draft storage; solution drafts live in per-person browser keepsakes (threads.js:112-196), initially empty; polish prompt also says to record and clear pre-existing box text. Mei-sees-empty-boxes leg cannot be pre-satisfied falsely by seed (no seeded drafts). (7) Seeded-read assertions are intended reads, not mutation probes, and match the seed exactly: Z/hro_restart Platform Engineer Applied Greta Lindqvist(1), Ade Bello(2), Marco Rossi(3); Screen Priya Nair(1), Samuel Ortiz(2); Noor APP-101 note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.'; Lena 1 unread = 3 APP-301 messages minus read_count 2; Noor long thread = 120 APP-101 messages (127 total minus 7 others), matching app_context.md. hro_restart's non-reload check ('starting data is not loaded again', 'no seeded record appears twice') is state-relative, so a reseeding app fails rather than passes. Weak-app attempt: an app that ignores writes but renders the seed cannot pass any mutation row because every proved mutation is keyed to a suffixed new job/card/text absent from the seed; a hard-coded seed copy fails the gate's unique-title readback. Conforming-alternative attempt: an app with different seeded IDs, routes or extra default content still passes because probes are judge-generated and suffixed and the prompt forbids relying on starting counts (prompt.md:15, app_context.md). No probe value found in seed_data.json or reference initial state. This is a static source review; no runtime was required for this row and none was exercised.
